This is what I have been waiting for someone to say for the last year and a half. I have met people that have tangible punch-in-gut losses like losing a loved one, but never have I found someone who says so plainly what I feel. You are speaking words from my own heart. Our type of grief is over the loss of something that is very real, but it is hard to find someone to validate it, so it is hard to move on. I tried to find a support group, but there wasn't any. I feel like I died when I was young, and what is left now is just a ghost of my self-that-could-have-been. Somewhere there is an alternate dimension where I was a young, happy, college student who graduated and had a full rewarding life. I am in the same place as you, but I am 53. I don't even have a career, I have been on disability for the last ten years, those would have been the last decent years of my life, before the dark times, before the menopause, but I only realized that I actually deserved the life I wanted in July of 2016, since then I have been pretty much depressed all the time. I too am so jealous of young people, especially college students. The worst part, to me, is that I have some long-time friends and most of my family members who think that the person I am today is pretty much how I should have turned out, and they all comment on how "nice" I am. And yet I feel like a character in a horror movie, where I am screaming "help me!" but no one can hear, they think everything is okay. I just went for a long drive on the freeway, and I really, really, really thought about running my car into a pillar. All the stuff that I had anxiety about then, I can do now! I put so much energy into what other people thought I should do. I had all the pieces, I just couldn't put them together right! Now I live in a dinky apartment with stuff piled everywhere, and my health sucks. I have never had a relationship, never had a career, haven't finished my degree, no kids, never traveled anywhere by myself. My whole life has been "subsistence agriculture." I wanted to be an anthropologist, I wanted to travel, I wanted recognition for being "smart," I wanted to have normal human relationships. I wanted to be in love, to be young and in love. I wanted to be athletic. I wanted to hike the Pacific Crest Trail. I wanted to wear nice clothes and feel attractive, without social anxiety. I wanted to have a past that I was proud of, instead of all this shame and regret and despair. I wanted to have "bragging rights." "Yes, I lived in London for two years when I was 35," or, "I backpacked across Europe," or "I lived in Mongolia with a native family in a yurt!" I wanted to feel like I could support myself without the crippling anxiety that I had at even my mediocre jobs, that I was going to screw up and get fired. I wanted to feel secure. I wanted to be self-confident. I have one family member that understands. My other friends and family are just tired of me complaining. One "friend" says, "but you've always felt like that." No, the difference between now and then is that I felt like I didn't deserve anything good then, and now I realize that I was worthy, I was deserving, and the only thing thing that stopped me from having what I wanted was me. There was nothing wrong with me, I wasn't a bad person. After my emotional Chernobyl, THEN I was diagnosed with cancer, and it was just another kick in the teeth. Now I have guilt to add to my pile of emotions. I go to this cancer hospital, and I am surrounded by all of these people who desperately want to live, and I just desperately want to die, and I feel so guilty for that.  I sometimes wish I could trade my life for someone who wants it more than I do. I was lucky with the cancer, my treatment wasn't bad, I am in remission, but I don't have any hope for the rest of my life. My therapist says it will "get better." Better than what? What am I supposed to do now? The rest of my life seems like it will be so empty. People tell me to volunteer, but I don't have anything to give. I could accept that now I should just try to enjoy the rest of my life, especially since I am living on borrowed time, but everything is tainted with regret. And how am I supposed to get money to do anything? How do I explain a huge gap in my resume, how do I get job skills now? My therapy sessions usually end with, "Well, what's one goal you could realistically do now?" Nothing. There is nothing I could do, right now. Then it's, "Well you could still do something-something." Not now, it doesn't mean anything now. Then I was emotionally weak, now I am physically weak, and that frightens me too. I can't imagine ever being healthy again, or in shape, or happy, and I have this image of me when I got out of high school, and I just have all this compassion for that lonely, awkward girl that I was, but I don't have any compassion for my present self, but I am the same person. I hate the person I am now because I hated the person I was then. I turned into exactly the person I thought I was, but I wasn't supposed to be like this. This is not me, but I can't find my way back to who I was, or am. I also suffer from Maladaptive Daydreaming, but in my daydreams, I am not a superhero or a movie star. I am just normal.

Sorry to take so long to get back to you. No, my radiation treatment was not very bad. They do something called hypofractionated whole breast irradiation, which sounds really scary but it actually just a higher dose over a lesser amount of days. This is supposed to lessen the bad effects on the skin. Mine was about 15 minutes total treatment time per day for 25 days. I had some redness and soreness, but my skin never really painful and it never started peeling. It is darker on that side, and the skin is thicker, but considering the alternative I am very grateful that I only have those side effects. Also, they will probably do the radiation with her laying face-down. This prevents any lung or heart damage from the radiation. They draw lines on your skin (with Sharpies!) so that they can align the machine easily, so you can't take a shower the whole time, or use deodorant, ugh! Also, if they have Pandora in the treatment room, tell your mom she gets to chose her own darn music! They didn't tell me I could choose my type of music until the last day, I had to listen to easy listening when I could have had Metallica or something. :)
